D0001.name: AsyncTreeSource
D0001.rationale: Async structural source correctly permits value-or-promise root/child resolution while retaining input hints and current output context; tree metadata remains forbidden.

D0002.name: AsyncTreeVisitor
D0002.rationale: Async tree visitor preserves phase-constrained commands and live input/output union; optional generic-order alignment is A17, not callback-timing unification.

D0003.name: ChildHintSorter
D0003.rationale: Returned hints replace expansion membership without a permutation constraint; sorter terminology underdescribes filtering, duplication and replacement.

D0004.name: AsyncChildHintSorter
D0004.rationale: Async sorter has the same unrestricted transform semantics; promises change execution timing, not the transformation contract.

D0005.name: KernelInspection
D0005.rationale: Kernel frames, owner epochs, ready visits, chain state and pending operations are detached diagnostics, not public scheduling extension points or restorable state.

D0006.name: InspectionFilters
D0006.rationale: emitEvents and visitorPhases represent genuinely independent controls; historical chain filters differ intentionally from delivery-time top-level filters.

D0007.name: DriverInspection
D0007.rationale: Driver inspection adds physical in-flight callback count to kernel diagnostics; it should not be interpreted as host-agent activity or independent execution control.

D0008.name: TreeDagExecutionInspection
D0008.rationale: Concrete tree/DAG inspection properly retains family phase typing and distinguishes buffered events from kernel boundaries; those counts must not be summed blindly.

D0009.name: TreeDagInspectionOperation
D0009.rationale: Operation literals correctly name the callback boundary; rename the sorting operation alongside its callback if A02 is accepted.

D0010.name: MutableRef
D0010.rationale: Standalone mutable reference explicitly exposes editing authority and generated ref identity; it is distinct from safe runner handles and arbitrary graph IDs.

D0011.name: VertexHandle
D0011.rationale: getValue/getRefId expose safe live handle capability; duplicate public VertexRef spelling collides with a reachable mutable internal alias but creates no leak.

D0012.name: OwnerToken
D0012.rationale: OwnerToken kind/id/epoch identify runner-local execution ownership, not caller vertices; reachable diagnostic support does not promise transferable capabilities.

D0013.name: VisitPhase
D0013.rationale: VisitPhase is a reachable tree/DAG engine union; general execution capabilities use configurable string phases and also support walking rather than this closed alias.

D0014.name: DagDiscoveryCycleError
D0014.rationale: Discovery error carries a frozen ordered closed witness; distinguish its payload name from structural SCC membership.

D0015.name: DagTraversalStallDiagnostics
D0015.rationale: Diagnostics retain original milestone constraints, unknown IDs and SCC membership; dependencyBlocked versus structurallyIncomplete distinguishes dependency and structural waits.

D0016.name: DagMilestone
D0016.rationale: Milestone pairs arbitrary vertex identity with work/subgraphCompletion, appropriately distinguishing W from C without claiming business outcomes.

D0017.name: DiagnosticId
D0017.rationale: DiagnosticId is a reachable inference-control helper, not a caller ID encoding or runtime conversion policy.

D0018.name: DagTraversalStallError
D0018.rationale: Stall error retains arbitrary IDs and exact diagnostic meaning; constructor compatibility for missing dependencyEdges is deliberate, not a missing runtime diagnostic.

D0019.name: DagWaitEdge
D0019.rationale: waiter/prerequisite and explicit reason literals correctly orient original W/C constraints, unlike ordinary walking from/to edges.

D0020.name: ExecutionInspection
D0020.rationale: Common inspection deliberately exposes only lifecycle/ownership fields; family-specific detail belongs in known concrete subtypes rather than widening this common interface.

D0021.name: VertexRef
D0021.rationale: Reachable internal VertexRef is mutable whereas the supported barrel alias means VertexHandle; consider InternalVertexRef to remove declaration-reader ambiguity.

D0022.name: VisitResult
D0022.rationale: VisitResult is transport support for family/phase-aware visitor results; undefined/void means no commands and does not itself mean deferred work.

D0023.name: StructuralChildEdge
D0023.rationale: Structural edges carry parent/child safe handles plus source hint position, distinct from work constraints and walking edges.

D0024.name: ChildSlot
D0024.rationale: Slot states accurately separate pending/live linkage/omission/deletion/disabled expansion; omission identity should match definition wrappers across layers.

D0025.name: HintVertexId
D0025.rationale: HintVertexId wraps the ID so a real undefined ID remains distinguishable from no known hint identity; retain this extra record.

D0026.name: ResolvedGraphVertex
D0026.rationale: Resolved graph records preserve current vertex, discovery depth, incoming edges, ordered slots and scheduling visit stage without exposing mutable containers.

D0027.name: ResolvedVisitStage
D0027.rationale: Visit stages describe scheduling boundaries rather than callback counts or W/C settlement; retain separate lifecycle vocabulary.

D0028.name: InternalStructuralChildEdge
D0028.rationale: Internal edge type is reachable implementation support; its mutable refs do not become supported public mutation authority through public structural-edge projection.

D0029.name: InternalChildSlot
D0029.rationale: Internal slot union leaks no linked mutable ref through ChildSlot's replacement branch; omitted own-ID presence remains an A14 cross-layer representation concern.

D0030.name: InternalResolvedGraphVertex
D0030.rationale: Internal graph-record fields support the public Omit/projection; private mutable facets must not be confused with safe ResolvedGraphVertex fields.

D0031.name: VisitorRecord
D0031.rationale: Visitor records contain detached wrapper metadata and shared callbacks; addedIndex and group identity are descriptive registration facts rather than configurable user indexes.

D0032.name: VertexId
D0032.rationale: VertexId intentionally means unknown because SameValueZero admits arbitrary identity; a string-only alias would incorrectly restrict current behavior.

D0033.name: MaybePromise
D0033.rationale: MaybePromise includes PromiseLike, matching async callback acceptance without promising asynchronous execution of every callback.

D0034.name: MutationCommand
D0034.rationale: MutationCommand restricts results to rewrite/delete/NOOP with family deletion parameter; generic replacement differs correctly from object-property patches.

D0035.name: MutationCommands
D0035.rationale: MutationCommands names the bound command-producing capability; it has a real configurable rewrite input and deletion family rather than a hidden object-only contract.

D0036.name: MutationCommandBuilder
D0036.rationale: Builder transforms typed mutation requests into commands; no implicit async, agent dispatch or storage contract is implied.

D0037.name: TreeMutationCommandBinder
D0037.rationale: Tree binder uses actual visitor arguments to bind tree-only deletion and output replacement; this is intentionally not a DAG mutation binder.

D0038.name: TreeMutationCommandBinderFactory
D0038.rationale: Factory creates typed tree binders under caller-specified configuration; generic name is supported by generic configuration and rewrite domains.

D0039.name: MutationRequest
D0039.rationale: rewrite/value, delete and keep are disjoint generic replacement requests; rejection-only patch fields prevent confusing them with object patch operations.

D0040.name: ResolvedGraphView
D0040.rationale: Graph view queries safe live state, all discovered identities and multiple structural paths; singular getRoot can be null for hidden-holder multi-entry sources, as documented.

D0041.name: OriginalGraphView
D0041.rationale: Original view retains progressively discovered first-accepted topology, not a complete deep source snapshot; omitted scheduling fields correctly avoid fabricated original progress.

D0042.name: TreeVertexMetadata
D0042.rationale: Tree metadata belongs to standalone mutable storage and carries resolution context; unlike runner observations, this advanced editing type intentionally permits mutation.

D0043.name: TreeVertexRecordContent
D0043.rationale: Standalone record content separates metadata/structural children from payload child hints; writable arrays are appropriate to this editing capability.

D0044.name: TreeVertexRecord
D0044.rationale: Tree record methods edit and clone standalone storage; they are not ordinary runner mutation methods, and children are structural references rather than hints.

D0045.name: ResolvedTreeMap
D0045.rationale: ResolvedTreeMap explicitly names a mutable Map for advanced storage; no ordinary runner getter exposes it as active engine authority.

D0046.name: GetPathToOptions
D0046.rationale: noRoot/noSelf are conventional exclusion flags with strict boolean validation; positive renaming is possible but weaker than ranked findings.

D0047.name: ResolvedTreeStore
D0047.rationale: ResolvedTreeStore intentionally supports direct editing, subtree deletion and source adaptation; asReadOnly gives a restricted view, with no public runner-store escape hatch.

D0048.name: VertexResolutionContext
D0048.rationale: VertexResolutionContext carries stable tree discovery position and non-null parent; synthetic DAG parent-nullability is introduced by the separate graph context union.

D0049.name: InternalVertexResolutionContext
D0049.rationale: Internal context retains mutable refs for standalone storage and engine transport; public resolution facets substitute restricted handles.

D0050.name: ResolvedTreeVertexTypes
D0050.rationale: ResolvedTreeVertexTypes truthfully describes a traversal of stored vertex references, with both data and hints being mutable standalone refs.

D0051.name: ResolvedTreeView
D0051.rationale: Tree query facade has one parent/path, frozen returned collections and live safe handles; absence and root context null are deliberate query results.

D0052.name: DagDiscoverySource
D0052.rationale: DAG discovery protocol distinguishes root/child resolution from optional prerequisite lookup and hint identity; current reference's retired lookup forms contradict the canonical tags.

D0053.name: AsyncDagDiscoverySource
D0053.rationale: Async DAG protocol preserves identical tagged results and ID domain through promises; no separate missing semantics should be inferred from async resolution.

D0054.name: DagChildResolutionContext
D0054.rationale: Graph child context explicitly hides synthetic source parent while preserving depth/index/hint; live and original graph views maintain different data domains.

D0055.name: RequiredGraphVertexIdentity
D0055.rationale: RequiredGraphVertexIdentity condition permits generated fallback only for default unknown domain; TypeScript cannot express own-property ownership but runtime validates it.

D0056.name: GraphDependencies
D0056.rationale: Dependency support type intentionally uses optional declaration lists; missing declaration policy differs from deliberate vertex omission.

D0057.name: DagVertexFound
D0057.rationale: Found result groups identity/declarations/content and requires explicit IDs for typed domains; generated-ID fallback does not turn output into arbitrary opaque data.

D0058.name: DagVertexOmitted
D0058.rationale: Omitted result explicitly acknowledges W/C satisfaction; its optional own identity is a different encoding from definition omission wrappers.

D0059.name: PrerequisiteMissing
D0059.rationale: missing is exclusive to prerequisite lookup; it is not omission or false work completion and current documentation should stop advertising undefined shorthand.

D0060.name: DagVertexResolution
D0060.rationale: Found/omitted union describes discovery resolution; preserving explicit tags avoids historical null ambiguities.

D0061.name: DagPrerequisiteResolution
D0061.rationale: Prerequisite union adds missing to canonical discovery results; retired undefined/null-content forms should remain rejected and documentation corrected.

D0062.name: TreeMetadataRestrictions
D0062.rationale: never-valued tree metadata keys are migration/rejection guards, not configurable fields or support for graph prerequisites on tree sources.

D0063.name: TreeChildResolutionContext
D0063.rationale: Tree child context correctly carries input/current union through parent context and live view while original view stays in input domain.

D0064.name: TreeVertexFound
D0064.rationale: Found tree result excludes identity/dependencies at both wrapper and vertex levels; nested vertexContent is uniform with DAG content despite verbosity.

D0065.name: TreeVertexOmitted
D0065.rationale: Tree omission has no dependency acknowledgment because tree-source semantics differ; do not mechanically add DAG satisfiesDependencies.

D0066.name: TreeVertexResolution
D0066.rationale: Tree resolution preserves found versus omitted and forbids graph metadata, including undefined own fields at runtime.

D0067.name: TreeSource
D0067.rationale: TreeSource is a structural callback protocol; input hints and current live context can be different domains without a nominal runtime base.

D0068.name: TraversalExecutionState
D0068.rationale: ExecutionState exposes observation and cooperative pause only; isHalted is lifecycle state, and getStopReason disambiguates prepared/paused/deferred stopping.

D0069.name: SyncTraversalExecution
D0069.rationale: Sync execution genuinely abstracts family-preserving run/iteration and selectors; this-return preserves concrete fluent methods and does not imply hidden session creation.

D0070.name: AsyncTraversalExecution
D0070.rationale: Async execution permits the same family-safe capability with Promise-this and async iterator ownership; no cancellation guarantee is advertised.

D0071.name: SelectedTraversalEvent
D0071.rationale: SelectedTraversalEvent narrows delivery discriminants while preserving facets; kind-first then phase fallback intentionally accommodates family record shapes.

D0072.name: TraversalStopReason
D0072.rationale: Stop reason is orthogonal to runner status and retains prepared/paused/awaitingSettlement distinctions; accepted settlement may preserve the prior reason until resume.

D0073.name: TraversalRunnerStatus
D0073.rationale: Status values describe engine lifecycle, not complete remote graph enumeration or business success; walkers additionally expose limited/closed outcomes.

D0074.name: TreeTraversalEvent
D0074.rationale: Tree events use phase and isTreeRoot because they observe traversal boundaries; they should not adopt DAG post-commit workCompleted labels.

D0075.name: TraversalExecutionOptions
D0075.rationale: Execution options independently patch emission and callback admission, with undefined retaining prior values; persisted options are documented, not call-local defaults.

D0076.name: EmissionKind
D0076.rationale: EmissionKind conditionally maps DAG phases to committed events while preserving arbitrary phase strings; explicit emitted-kind type remains available to generic wrappers.

D0077.name: VisitorPhaseSelection
D0077.rationale: all/include/exclude selection is a real caller choice and handles empty lists without conflating no callbacks with no events.

D0078.name: TreeVisitorRecord
D0078.rationale: TreeVisitorRecord correctly pairs phase-sensitive callback with shared normalized registration metadata; detached list results are not live registrations.

D0079.name: TreeVisitor
D0079.rationale: TreeVisitor safely constrains commands by phase/family but places phase first unlike DAG/walking aliases; optional consistency change is limited to generic order.

D0080.name: VisitorInputs
D0080.rationale: VisitorInputs maps normalized records to accepted registration input, not engine internals; undefined phases are field-wise no-change patches.

D0081.name: TraversalVisitorCommandArguments
D0081.rationale: Command argument algebra enforces operation-specific payloads; newHints unnecessarily requires mutable input arrays despite source-domain ownership semantics.

D0082.name: TraversalVisitorCommand
D0082.rationale: Discriminated commandName/commandArguments pair preserves required payloads and forbidden no-argument fields; no generic unvalidated command object is exposed.

D0083.name: NoInferPhase
D0083.rationale: NoInferPhase is inference support preventing visitor widening of the chosen phase; it is not an executable policy knob.

D0084.name: HintCommand
D0084.rationale: HintCommand is a reachable phase-restriction alias for rewriting source hints; no additional public operation or binding exists.

D0085.name: DeletionCommandName
D0085.rationale: Deletion names deliberately distinguish structural tree subtree from DAG dependency cascade; generic mutation types carry this family parameter.

D0086.name: CommonCommand
D0086.rationale: CommonCommand subtracts hint/deferral/deletion variants before reconstructing family-safe results; it does not export new runtime commands.

D0087.name: TraversalVisitorResult
D0087.rationale: VisitorResult makes deferral an exclusive one-command result and restricts hint rewrites by phase; generic defaults do not override concrete family restrictions.

D0088.name: TreeVisitorContext
D0088.rationale: Tree context separately names phase index, visitor index, preceding phase vertex, chain-local state and registration; none represents external work attempts.

D0089.name: TraversalVisitorCommandName
D0089.rationale: Command enum is descriptive and family-specific; pause is resumable, deletion cascades are explicit, and skip affects pending expansion rather than already resolved children.

D0090.name: CommandCommitMode
D0090.rationale: afterEachVisitor/afterGroup controls command visibility independently of concurrency; actual grouped callback ordering is explicit elsewhere.

D0091.name: TraversalVisitorFunctionOptions
D0091.rationale: priority orders callbacks within registrations, not DAG task scheduling; function options and contextual placement already scope that generic noun sufficiently.

D0092.name: VisitorDefinition
D0092.rationale: VisitorDefinition accepts shorthand or metadata wrapper; bare callback convenience does not erase priority/group behavior in normalized output.

D0093.name: VisitorGroupMember
D0093.rationale: Group members can set local priority but cannot override group commit policy; resolutionStyle never fields enforce removed compatibility rather than promise support.

D0094.name: VisitorGroupDefinition
D0094.rationale: Explicit groups own member order/batching and allow real policy selection; empty validated groups being inert is intentional.

D0095.name: VisitorPhaseInput
D0095.rationale: Phase input spans callback/flat definitions/ordered groups consistently across builder APIs, avoiding duplicate registration configuration concepts.

D0096.name: VisitorGroupMetadata
D0096.rationale: Group metadata identity is runner/registration-local descriptive data; explicit flag distinguishes authored group boundaries from implicit batching.

D0097.name: VisitorRegistrationMetadata
D0097.rationale: Registration metadata omits callable visitor while retaining descriptive indexes and group policy; clients use listVisitorsFor for full typed records.

D0098.name: VertexTypes
D0098.rationale: VertexTypes names data/hint domains independently; opaque defaults prevent business-schema assumptions and input hints remain the source contract.

D0099.name: VertexCloneContent
D0099.rationale: Clone input supports own data undefined and optional hints; clone output must honor the independent collection promise consistently on standalone Vertex.

D0100.name: Vertex
D0100.rationale: Standalone Vertex permits mutable hints intentionally, but structural compatibility with VertexView means clone must copy rather than alias its hint collection.

D0101.name: VertexContent
D0101.rationale: Content describes mutable standalone payload/hints; source input should be split if readonly authored hint arrays are accepted without changing mutable output authority.

D0102.name: VertexView
D0102.rationale: Safe view separates live payload observation from mutable editing; runner facets copy clone hints correctly, while structurally assignable standalone Vertex does not.

D0103.name: VertexContentInput
D0103.rationale: Input rejects legacy spellings and currently inherits mutable hint-array requirement; accepting readonly inputs should define ownership explicitly.

D0104.name: materializeDagInputFromRoots
D0104.rationale: Materialize-from-roots accurately names eager discovery of record-valued children and returns an input envelope, not a source protocol.

D0105.name: materializeDagInputFromRootsAsync
D0105.rationale: Async roots materializer awaits selectors/enumeration then returns a reusable synchronous envelope; Async describes construction, not returned callback necessity.

D0106.name: materializeDagInputFromRecords
D0106.rationale: Record materializer catalogs every record and ID-valued structural relations; materialize/Input naming correctly distinguishes it from lazy discovery.

D0107.name: materializeDagInputFromRecordsAsync
D0107.rationale: Async record materializer captures catalog membership once and preserves shallow data/ID identity; no hidden durable snapshot or checkpoint is promised.

D0108.name: DagRecordSelectors
D0108.rationale: Record selector id and children/dependency functions are contextual operations; children yielding IDs is distinct from root-selector record-valued children by type.

D0109.name: DagRootSelectors
D0109.rationale: Root selectors deliberately replace the children result domain with records; generic selectors retain opaque data identity and W/C lists are still IDs.

D0110.name: AsyncCollection
D0110.rationale: AsyncCollection accepts either sync or async iterable; values themselves need not be promises, which is correctly separated from MaybePromise callbacks.

D0111.name: AsyncDagRecordSelectors
D0111.rationale: Async selectors permit promised IDs and iterable relations while preserving operation names; absent selectors mean empty lists, not deferred unresolved edges.

D0112.name: AsyncDagRootSelectors
D0112.rationale: Async roots selectors yield records for expansion and reuse W/C ID selectors; preserving that materialization distinction is preferable to one ambiguous children type.

D0113.name: MaterializedDagInput
D0113.rationale: MaterializedDagInput faithfully contains traversableGraph plus mandatory syntheticRoot; generic resolveChild accepts rewritten current context without changing captured source data.

D0114.name: ObjectRewriteContext
D0114.rationale: Rewrite context carries classification and path helpers as observations, not configure options; input/output key union and unknown current values are necessary.

D0115.name: ObjectRewriteInput
D0115.rationale: Current rewrite input admits assembledComposite and unknown mixed value; it must not pretend post-order reconstruction preserves narrow input/output value unions.

D0116.name: ObjectRewriteCallback
D0116.rationale: Rewrite callback returns property patch/delete/keep with unknown intermediate values; keep legitimately assembles processed children and is not generic NOOP.

D0117.name: RewriteObjectResult
D0117.rationale: Temporal outputAtReturn/getOutput distinction is correct, but null collapses absent root and retained null; expose presence separately if needed.

D0118.name: RewriteObjectOptions
D0118.rationale: Owned-source rewrite options reject traversableTree and support classifiers/assemblers; current reference incorrectly adds classification/path observations as options.

D0119.name: RootValueConverter
D0119.rationale: Converter complete flag identifies capture timing but not root presence; null-before-conversion collapses deletion with a retained null value.

D0120.name: rewriteObject
D0120.rationale: rewriteObject appropriately defaults output unknown and runs post-order assembly; result presence ambiguity is distinct from its already-correct completion gate.

D0121.name: rewriteObjectAs
D0121.rationale: rewriteObjectAs explicitly asserts output type without validation; adding a presence result should preserve that assertion boundary and not claim type checking.

D0122.name: __TRAVERSABLE_OBJECT_TREE_DEFAULT_ROOT_KEY__
D0122.rationale: Root-key constant is declaration-reachable through mapper return types but has no supported exported binding; historical public-export rename finding is rejected.

D0123.name: createRootPropertyMapper
D0123.rationale: Default mapper overload preserves exact input value and literal default key; its public access is through ObjectTreeSource static, not a free export.

D0124.name: createRootPropertyMapper
D0124.rationale: Key-supplied mapper overload preserves caller key type; it is one overload of the same static capability, not an independent API issue.

D0125.name: createRootPropertyMapper
D0125.rationale: Optional-key mapper overload accurately unions default and supplied key identity; rename coordination should preserve all overload inference.

D0126.name: getChildrenOfPropertyDefault
D0126.rationale: Default child enumerator returns PropertyKey/unknown properties and is a class static; possible operation-oriented naming does not create a nonexistent free-export duplicate.

D0127.name: ObjectAssemblyCache
D0127.rationale: Cache has/get/set is structural and may use non-Map storage; unknown writes are required for mixed assembled composites.

D0128.name: ObjectMutationOptions
D0128.rationale: Real options permit classification/assembly/cache policies; dual classifier precedence and cache terminology merit findings, but isComposite is not configurable today.

D0129.name: ObjectMutationRequest
D0129.rationale: Object requests use patch rather than generic value replacement; keep retains the property while assembling processed children, an intentional scoped transformation.

D0130.name: ObjectPropertyPatch
D0130.rationale: Property patch is limited to key/value and preserves metadata; unknown own fields reject, and explicit undefined value differs from absence.

D0131.name: ObjectMutationCommands
D0131.rationale: Bound mutation commands also expose composite assembly; saveToMap boolean should make cache-result policy clearer without changing classifier or command semantics.

D0132.name: ObjectMutationBinder
D0132.rationale: Object binder uses full tree visitor context and current mixed domain, correctly returning tree-only deletion commands rather than business mutations.

D0133.name: ObjectMutationBinderFactory
D0133.rationale: Object binder factory configures classifiers, assemblers and cache; its generic domain parameters describe input/requested output rather than asserted final homogeneous values.

D0134.name: createObjectMutationBinder
D0134.rationale: Mutation binder is legitimately exported both free and static; unlike mapper/enumerator this duplication exists, but convenience alone is too weak for a separate ranked defect.

D0135.name: PropertyMetadata
D0135.rationale: PropertyMetadata distributively removes key/value to preserve metadata alternatives; it is reachable type machinery, not metadata stripping during execution.

D0136.name: ObjectCurrentVertexTypes
D0136.rationale: ObjectCurrentVertexTypes intentionally widens current values to unknown while retaining keys and metadata alternatives; input hints remain tied to discovery source domain.

D0137.name: ObjectTreeVertexTypes
D0137.rationale: Object tree types model both data and hints as property records; this is why precise source adapters are required for narrowed domains.

D0138.name: ObjectCompositeClassification
D0138.rationale: Composite flags may overlap while assembly prefers array; document or replace with one tagged classifier, and do not advertise isComposite as an input hook.

D0139.name: TraversableObject
D0139.rationale: TraversableObject models nested arrays/records rather than preserving arbitrary prototypes; custom source/assembly adapters provide actual broader policy where needed.

D0140.name: TraversableObjectProp
D0140.rationale: Property key/value records intentionally allow null/undefined values and opaque metadata through surrounding types; no implicit deletion is encoded in value.

D0141.name: TraversableObjectPropKey
D0141.rationale: Property key union matches JS string/number/symbol keys; symbols retain identity and numeric normalization belongs to reconstruction policy.

D0142.name: ObjectTreeBaseOptions
D0142.rationale: Root mapper and child enumerator have different operations from tagged child resolution hook; shorter operation-oriented names could make that separation easier to find.

D0143.name: ObjectTreePropertyAdapters
D0143.rationale: Precise property adapters require root and child functions together, protecting narrow K/V inference; requiredness should survive any naming cleanup.

D0144.name: ObjectTreeOptions
D0144.rationale: ObjectTreeOptions conditionally requires adapters for narrow domains; generic flexibility is real through callbacks, not an unchecked type assertion.

D0145.name: ObjectChildHookResult
D0145.rationale: Child hook useDefault/found/omitted distinguishes delegation from custom resolution and rejects graph metadata; it applies only to children by design.

D0146.name: ObjectTreeSource
D0146.rationale: Source constructor/fromProperties enforce typed adapters; static mapper/enumerator are actual public access routes and mutation binder also has a free route.

D0147.name: AsyncBreadthFirstTreeTraversal
D0147.rationale: Async BFS class is a reusable configurable builder with phase-safe registration snapshots; builder suffix is optional churn weaker than ranked findings.

D0148.name: BreadthFirstTreeTraversal
D0148.rationale: BFS class configures source/registrations and creates independent runners; no immediate execution in construction is promised by current documented pattern.

D0149.name: AsyncBreadthFirstTreeOptionsPatch
D0149.rationale: Async BFS patch owns source/sorter/visitors/retention/concurrency and validates atomically; only sorter name underdescribes membership replacement.

D0150.name: AsyncBreadthFirstTreeOptions
D0150.rationale: Async BFS full options require source while patch fields remain optional; callback concurrency is real, unlike unsupported walking concurrency.

D0151.name: AsyncBreadthFirstTraversalVisitors
D0151.rationale: Async BFS registration map is phase-keyed normalized records; it is not a public global queue or cross-phase priority order.

D0152.name: AsyncBreadthFirstTreeRunner
D0152.rationale: Async BFS runner exposes both tree and graph query facades without mutable storage; concrete inspection retains BFS phase and cooperative pause semantics.

D0153.name: BreadthFirstTreeOptionsPatch
D0153.rationale: Sync BFS patch preserves source and supports nullable sorter clearing; transformer naming should be consistent with its actual replacement capability.

D0154.name: BreadthFirstTreeOptions
D0154.rationale: Sync BFS full options require the structural tree source and inherit correct registration/retention policy; no graph IDs can be injected through tree results.

D0155.name: BreadthFirstPhase
D0155.rationale: Single LEVEL_ORDER phase matches BFS callback boundaries; absence of DFS in/post order is a family distinction, not missing configuration.

D0156.name: BreadthFirstTreeRunner
D0156.rationale: Sync BFS runner retains family-safe execution and safe tree/root queries; it does not expose isTraversalLeaf's ambiguous DFS convenience.

D0157.name: BreadthFirstTraversalVisitors
D0157.rationale: BFS visitor map accurately scopes callbacks to level order and current data; flat/group registration inputs are provided by the mapped input helper.

D0158.name: traverseTreeBreadthFirst
D0158.rationale: traverseTreeBreadthFirst runs immediately and returns its resumable runner; one options object prevents duplicated source arguments.

D0159.name: traverseTreeBreadthFirstAsync
D0159.rationale: Async BFS helper awaits run and returns runner; Async suffix consistently marks helper execution rather than a different output data model.

D0160.name: AsyncDagTraversal
D0160.rationale: Async DAG builder accepts sync or async graph protocol with correct inference, tree source restrictions and graph-only trailing ID domain.

D0161.name: DagWorkTicket
D0161.rationale: Work ticket intentionally exposes only vertexId with hidden nominal provenance; it is not a persisted task claim or transferable attempt record.

D0162.name: DagWorkBoundary
D0162.rationale: Advance boundary distinguishes awaiting settlement, explicit pause and finish; work tickets exist only at deferred dispatch boundary, not committed event delivery.

D0163.name: DagSettlementReceipt
D0163.rationale: Settlement receipt names accepted versus identical replay clearly; it is an acknowledgment of traversal state, not business success or durable acceptance.

D0164.name: DagCoordinationControl
D0164.rationale: Shared session control delegates DAG inspection but types it only as general execution state; specialize known inspection while preserving generic capabilities elsewhere.

D0165.name: DagWorkSession
D0165.rationale: Sync work session advances/settles/observes a DAG; detailed inspection erasure is avoidable and ticket provenance remains session-facade local.

D0166.name: AsyncDagWorkSession
D0166.rationale: Async session changes advance to Promise while settlement stays synchronous; preserving this distinction avoids false assumptions of asynchronous acceptance.

D0167.name: createDagWorkSession
D0167.rationale: Free session factory wraps existing runner progress and owns only facade-local tickets; distinguish its name from independent prepared factory creation.

D0168.name: createAsyncDagWorkSession
D0168.rationale: Async free factory also wraps the existing owner/session rather than cloning execution; wrapping terminology should align with sync counterpart.

D0169.name: NominalDagWorkTicket
D0169.rationale: Nominal ticket class is type-only provenance support with no public runtime constructor; copying fields cannot forge a valid ticket.

D0170.name: composeDag
D0170.rationale: Composition joins instance definitions and explicit wires but does not enforce provenance of an instantiated object; mapped fragment naming should reflect structural equivalence.

D0171.name: defineDagFragment
D0171.rationale: defineDagFragment validates a closed graph and ports, unlike shape-normalizing defineDag; retain validation but clarify the inconsistent define verb guarantee.

D0172.name: instantiateDagFragment
D0172.rationale: Instantiation actually remaps all declared IDs once and preserves shallow data; no additional runtime instance identity is established.

D0173.name: DagTraversal
D0173.rationale: DAG builder configures sources/visitors and creates runners; source family cannot change via configure, consistent with its validated options contract.

D0174.name: defineDag
D0174.rationale: defineDag copies/freezes topology and normalizes lists without graph semantic validation; normalizeDagDefinition would state the narrower guarantee.

D0175.name: diffDagDefinitions
D0175.rationale: Definition diff explicitly reports shallow data identity and ordered declaration changes; it does not infer artifact invalidation, so retain the scoped definition name.

D0176.name: filterAsyncDagDataVisitor
D0176.rationale: Async filtered data visitor supports promise callbacks with synchronous type-guard predicate; type narrowing and family/phase restrictions are retained.

D0177.name: filterAsyncDagDataVisitor
D0177.rationale: Boolean-predicate overload filters without narrowing; it is the same helper and should not be counted as another behavior or another finding.

D0178.name: FilteredVisitor
D0178.rationale: FilteredVisitor receives data rather than Vertex plus ordinary DAG context; reachable alias reflects wrapper callback shape and does not create a new public visitor family.

D0179.name: AsyncFilteredVisitor
D0179.rationale: Async filtered callback returns the async visitor result domain while predicate stays sync; this distinction is documented and no separate exported alias is required.

D0180.name: filterDagDataVisitor
D0180.rationale: Sync filter helper narrows data with a predicate but does not defer skipped work; externalSettlement remains the real completion-policy control.

D0181.name: filterDagDataVisitor
D0181.rationale: Boolean predicate overload preserves data domain without assertion; false produces no commands and still follows configured work-completion semantics.

D0182.name: hasSingleStructuralSink
D0182.rationale: hasSingleStructuralSink explicitly counts no-structural-child vertices; it avoids the ambiguous general graph sink vocabulary and ignores W/C edges correctly.

D0183.name: inspectDagMilestones
D0183.rationale: inspectDagMilestones captures an observational synchronous snapshot from either runner family; it never advances execution or claims live-refresh semantics.

D0184.name: AsyncDagSource
D0184.rationale: AsyncDagSource is a reachable source-option envelope, not a named supported public import; do not report it as a falsely named exported source protocol.

D0185.name: AsyncDagTraversalVisitors
D0185.rationale: Async DAG registration map preserves phase and trailing ID domain; empty/filtered callbacks still follow external versus automatic work-completion policy.

D0186.name: AsyncDagTraversalOptionsInput
D0186.rationale: Reachable options input groups graph scheduling and callbacks; sorter transform and undeclared-work default names are cross-family concerns, not separate async defects.

D0187.name: AsyncDagOptions
D0187.rationale: Async DAG options require exactly one source and exclude graph policies for tree sources; patch semantics and ID inference retain family constraints.

D0188.name: AsyncDagOptionsPatch
D0188.rationale: Async patch can replace an adapter within its original family and cannot silently switch tree to graph; undefined retains fields atomically.

D0189.name: AsyncDagTraversalRunner
D0189.rationale: Async runner exposes guarded synchronous settlement despite async execution; accepting the emitted ID/generation record could simplify callers without changing guards.

D0190.name: DagDefinitionVertex
D0190.rationale: Definition vertex explicitly stores data, ordered structural slots and separate W/C dependencies; all required lists make authored topology unambiguous.

D0191.name: DagDefinition
D0191.rationale: Definition includes ordered live declarations, known omissions and root/roots/empty entry; it represents source facts rather than progress or executable validity.

D0192.name: DagDefinitionIssue
D0192.rationale: Issue kinds correctly separate structural/semantic failures, but structuralCycle and discoveryCycle vertexIds carry incompatible SCC/witness evidence and need clearer field names.

D0193.name: DagDefinitionSlot
D0193.rationale: Omitted slots explicitly wrap identity or null, accurately preserving undefined IDs; align other omission-bearing public layers with this representation if changing them.

D0194.name: PrepareDagResult
D0194.rationale: Preparation result exposes an executable prepared DAG only on valid branch; invalid issue arrays preserve exact graph domain without top-level diagnostic aliases.

D0195.name: InferredDagId
D0195.rationale: InferredDagId constrains option inference so foreign wires cannot widen IDs; it is reachable compile-time plumbing rather than an identity mapper.

D0196.name: DagFragment
D0196.rationale: Fragment is definition plus typed named live ports with shallow data; no nominal provenance separates it from the instance alias.

D0197.name: DagFragmentInstance
D0197.rationale: Instance alias is structurally identical to fragment; rename/remove the unenforced distinction rather than inventing a current instance invariant.

D0198.name: DagCompositionOptions
D0198.rationale: Composition dependencies wire a live dependent to explicit W/C milestone, while children add structure separately; generic dependencies is justified by actual milestone selection.

D0199.name: DagFragmentValidationError
D0199.rationale: Fragment validation error exposes definition issues and preserves arbitrary IDs; catch narrowing does not recover generic identity type automatically.

D0200.name: DagMilestoneStatus
D0200.rationale: Milestone status separates live satisfaction from omitted/deleted/unresolved identities; work state alone does not prove C is satisfied.

D0201.name: WorkTarget
D0201.rationale: WorkTarget is a reachable discriminant narrowing for terminal unfinished-work blockers; target requires the same arbitrary ID semantics as queries.

D0202.name: CompletionTarget
D0202.rationale: CompletionTarget scopes discovery-open/completion-pending blockers to C; it should not be exposed as a different vertex identity scheme.

D0203.name: DagBlocker
D0203.rationale: Blockers form a causal constraint graph plus terminal facts, not an ordered execution plan; reason/status fields preserve W/C and local discovery distinctions.

D0204.name: DagMilestoneQueryOptions
D0204.rationale: transitive is an actual configurable query policy with deterministic traversal; it does not imply source discovery or automatic recursion into host data.

D0205.name: DagExplanation
D0205.rationale: Explanation distinguishes unknown/deleted/known and reports discovery completeness; known omitted identities legitimately have null progress and satisfied milestones.

D0206.name: DagMilestoneSnapshot
D0206.rationale: Milestone snapshot methods query one capture and do not refresh after settlement; Snapshot naming correctly contrasts with live graph views.

D0207.name: DagMilestoneQueryResult
D0207.rationale: Query result returns milestones plus original oriented edges and capture completeness; dependent queries do not reverse the waiter's edge representation.

D0208.name: DagWorkState
D0208.rationale: Work states describe engine eligibility/callback/deferral/commit, not host attempts; visiting must not be read as remote agent running.

D0209.name: DagVertexProgress
D0209.rationale: Progress exposes separate W and C unmet sets and their union; generation belongs only to deferred work and optional presence is appropriate.

D0210.name: DagSettlementGeneration
D0210.rationale: Generation is a local symbol guard, not a monotonic durable generation number; domain-scoped type/documentation adequately state its nonpersistent meaning.

D0211.name: DagSummary
D0211.rationale: DAG summary collections overlap intentionally and distinguish deferred work from active callback vertices; summary is observational, not a dispatch claim service.

D0212.name: DagDeferredWork
D0212.rationale: Deferred work pairs vertexId and generation atomically; low-level settlement should accept that record directly instead of requiring positional recombination.

D0213.name: DagSettlementOutcome
D0213.rationale: workCompleted versus traversalFailed distinguishes accepted traversal work from fatal whole-runner failure; per-attempt failure/retry remains host policy.

D0214.name: DagRevisionResult
D0214.rationale: Revision result returns fresh prepared graph and changes only on valid branch; it carries no implicit migration of old tickets or accepted facts.

D0215.name: DagDefinitionChangeAspect
D0215.rationale: Diff aspects use relation nouns appropriate to change descriptions, unlike dependsOn verbs on declarations; no cosmetic unification is necessary.

D0216.name: DagDefinitionVertexChange
D0216.rationale: Changed vertex records report ID plus ordered aspects, not full replacement data or semantic business invalidation.

D0217.name: DagDefinitionDiff
D0217.rationale: Definition diff reports shallow data changes, ordered vertex membership and entry/omission changes; it is intentionally not a deep durable-state diff.

D0218.name: DagRevisionOperation
D0218.rationale: removeVertexDeclaration explicitly avoids cascade semantics while replace/add operations use full declarations; ordered batch validation permits repaired intermediate dangling links.

D0219.name: DagSchedulingOptions
D0219.rationale: Work completion/discovery/root policies are real choices; omittedWorkDependencies specifically concerns absent declarations and collides with omitted-vertex terminology.

D0220.name: DagSource
D0220.rationale: DagSource is an unexported reachable options envelope, not the actual DagDiscoverySource protocol; absence of a public binding invalidates the candidate rename finding.

D0221.name: DagTraversalVisitors
D0221.rationale: DAG visitor map preserves W-ready/C-ready phase semantics independently of emission kinds; registration policies affect callbacks, not host work ordering.

D0222.name: DagTraversalOptionsInput
D0222.rationale: Reachable DAG input options expose the same hint transform and missing-declaration default policies; no hidden public normalized-options injection is available.

D0223.name: DagOptions
D0223.rationale: DAG full options enforce one source and graph-only dependency policies; proposed naming changes should preserve strict own-key and source-family checks.

D0224.name: DagOptionsPatch
D0224.rationale: DAG patch represents future-runner changes within fixed source family; undefined is retain, not clearing, and atomic validation prevents partial updates.

D0225.name: DagVisitorPhase
D0225.rationale: ON_WORK_READY and ON_SUBGRAPH_READY are callback admission phases, deliberately different from committed workCompleted/subgraphCompleted events.

D0226.name: DagTraversalRunner
D0226.rationale: Sync DAG runner supplies prepare/settle/summary plus safe views; atomic deferred-record settlement would reduce caller mistakes while preserving its lifecycle.

D0227.name: DagVisitor
D0227.rationale: DAG visitor generic order differs from tree phase-first aliases; actual payload, ID flow and command restrictions are otherwise coherent and should remain separate.

D0228.name: AsyncDagVisitor
D0228.rationale: Async DAG visitor keeps the same domain/domain/phase/ID ordering and allows value-or-promise returns; generic alignment is a coordinated optional tree-side change.

D0229.name: DagEvent
D0229.rationale: DAG events use committed milestone kind, arbitrary vertex ID and historical vertex facet; they are observations after work and must not dispatch it.

D0230.name: DagVisitorContext
D0230.rationale: DAG context supplies live/original graph views and callback chain metadata; root flag refers to actual visible container root, not every synthetic entry.

D0231.name: OwnedOptions
D0231.rationale: OwnedOptions never fields deliberately reject topology/source overrides in prepared factories; these fields are unavailable configuration, not options callers can enable.

D0232.name: PreparedDagRunnerOptions
D0232.rationale: Prepared sync runner options permit visitors/seeds/work completion/retention while topology remains owned; this justified restriction protects reusable validation.

D0233.name: PreparedAsyncDagRunnerOptions
D0233.rationale: Prepared async runner additionally exposes callback concurrency and returns a prepared runner promise; source materialization is not replayed.

D0234.name: DagWorkSessionOptions
D0234.rationale: Work-session options own external settlement and forbid visitors; customize a runner then wrap it when callback dispatch is needed.

D0235.name: AsyncDagWorkSessionOptions
D0235.rationale: Async work-session options add concurrency without opening source/topology overrides; accepted completion seed copies remain independent across prepared sessions.

D0236.name: PreparedDag
D0236.rationale: Prepared factory creates independent runners/sessions, unlike free wrappers over one runner; definition and lossy live-child projection remain intentionally distinct.

D0237.name: PreparedDagVertex
D0237.rationale: Prepared vertex children omit omission slots and are a convenience projection, not serialization; faithful definition is explicitly available for reconstruction.

D0238.name: PrepareDagInput
D0238.rationale: Preparation input requires a DAG discovery protocol and fixed eager preview policies, with no visitor/source-family injection capability.

D0239.name: PrepareAsyncDagInput
D0239.rationale: Async preparation accepts the async protocol plus concurrency; result still captures topology into reusable synchronous in-memory definitions.

D0240.name: prepareDag
D0240.rationale: prepareDag discovers and validates into valid/invalid result while exact source errors throw; this source preparation is distinct from mutating runner.prepare.

D0241.name: prepareDagAsync
D0241.rationale: Async preparation overload for sync protocol preserves inference and still returns a promise; it is not a second semantic preparation path.

D0242.name: prepareDagAsync
D0242.rationale: Async-protocol overload is part of the same helper and accepts promise-like callbacks; never count overload declarations as separate findings.

D0243.name: PrepareDagOptions
D0243.rationale: Preparation options correctly reject execution fields; absent dependency-declaration policy should be renamed consistently with DAG scheduling if A06 is accepted.

D0244.name: prepareDagDefinition
D0244.rationale: Definition preparation validates source facts without callbacks and returns executable topology only if valid; normalizeDagDefinition would clarify the preceding shape-only step.

D0245.name: RevisionDomain
D0245.rationale: RevisionDomain prevents operation data/ID widening; reachable inference helper should not be sold as revision serialization or persistence.

D0246.name: reviseDag
D0246.rationale: reviseDag validates ordered candidate changes atomically and returns a new prepared value; it does not cancel/migrate old execution or infer accepted work.

D0247.name: traverseDag
D0247.rationale: traverseDag immediately runs a configured DAG and returns a resumable runner; generic name is scoped by DAG and explicitly selectable scheduling policies.

D0248.name: traverseDagAsync
D0248.rationale: Async DAG helper preserves source/current/ID inference with promised completion of its run boundary; settlement remains a separate host-controlled operation.

D0249.name: AsyncDepthFirstTreeTraversal
D0249.rationale: Async DFS builder shares source/registration/configuration snapshot semantics; optional builder suffix would be broad churn without stronger evidence than ranked findings.

D0250.name: DepthFirstTreeTraversal
D0250.rationale: DFS builder supports configured in-order boundaries and all three phases before creating independent runners; conventional class naming is retainable.

D0251.name: ChildIndexSelection
D0251.rationale: Child selection distinguishes indices from inclusive ranges with negative endpoints; actual policy configurability justifies generic boundary selection rather than binary-tree-only naming.

D0252.name: AsyncDepthFirstTraversalVisitors
D0252.rationale: Async DFS visitor map preserves phase-sensitive result restrictions; command order and async concurrency remain independent policies.

D0253.name: AsyncDepthFirstTreeOptionsPatch
D0253.rationale: Async DFS options expose real concurrency and in-order policy; sorter naming should become transform terminology consistently across this family.

D0254.name: AsyncDepthFirstTreeOptions
D0254.rationale: Async DFS full options require tree source while patch remains source-preserving; no graph metadata or runtime base class is required.

D0255.name: AsyncDepthFirstTreeRunner
D0255.rationale: Async DFS isTraversalLeaf uses disabled-or-hintless logic rather than resolved structural leaf, matching the sync ambiguity; other view/root capabilities remain clear.

D0256.name: DepthFirstFrameStage
D0256.rationale: Frame stages are reachable implementation diagnostics, not public configurable traversal phases; no need to rename every internal scheduling stage as a supported API.

D0257.name: InOrderOptions
D0257.rationale: In-order options explicitly select boundaries, fallback, one-child behavior and omission behavior; generic in-order is justified by actual n-ary policy controls.

D0258.name: InOrderOptionsPatch
D0258.rationale: In-order patch makes every field optional/undefined-retaining and validates resulting ranges; it does not replace the entire in-order configuration like walk limits.

D0259.name: DepthFirstTreeOptionsPatch
D0259.rationale: Sync DFS patch supports real in-order/custom hint transformation; source/visitor snapshots remain future-runner configuration, not active runner mutation.

D0260.name: DepthFirstTreeOptions
D0260.rationale: DFS full options require exactly a tree source and inherit patch policies; retained original structure remains progressively discovered and shallow.

D0261.name: DepthFirstPhase
D0261.rationale: PRE_ORDER/IN_ORDER/POST_ORDER correctly identify callback/event boundaries; CTT allows several in-order occurrences for configured n-ary child boundaries.

D0262.name: DepthFirstTreeRunner
D0262.rationale: isTraversalLeaf can disagree with final resolved child count in both directions; separate hintlessness, skipped expansion and actual resolved leaf queries.

D0263.name: DepthFirstTraversalVisitors
D0263.rationale: DFS visitors map the family phase enum to typed records, with input mappings supporting flat/group policies; no generic callback phase widening is necessary.

D0264.name: traverseTreeDepthFirst
D0264.rationale: Depth-first convenience helper executes immediately with canonical single options object; no extra source argument or hidden continuation injection is supported.

D0265.name: traverseTreeDepthFirstAsync
D0265.rationale: Async depth-first helper returns a promised runner after its execution boundary, retaining pause/resume and exact error behavior.

D0266.name: AsyncGraphWalk
D0266.rationale: Async walking builder is legitimately configurable for strategy/revisit/predicates/visitors/limits and serial execution; concurrency absence is explicit, not an unimplemented knob.

D0267.name: AsyncGraphWalkRunner
D0267.rationale: Async walker extends common execution with terminal close and summary; iterator return remains resumable pause and close disposal is a separate operation.

D0268.name: GraphWalk
D0268.rationale: GraphWalk configures truly selectable exploration policies over its own source protocol; it is not a misleading universal arbitrary graph adapter.

D0269.name: GraphWalkEvent
D0269.rationale: Walking union accurately distinguishes vertex occurrence, followed edge and path prefix; source in an edge event means source vertex and depth refers to target route.

D0270.name: GraphWalkEdge
D0270.rationale: Walking edge from/outgoingIndex/to/data identifies a directed adjacency occurrence before filtering; arbitrary caller edge data retains identity.

D0271.name: GraphWalkEventFor
D0271.rationale: EventFor narrows by walking phase/kind, preserving data and ID; it should not be merged with callback types or CTT W/C event timing.

D0272.name: GraphWalkPathEvent
D0272.rationale: Path event is a typed route-prefix observation, not a promise of only terminal paths; revisit policy controls which prefixes occur.

D0273.name: GraphWalkOperation
D0273.rationale: Walking operations distinguish source callback, iterator next/return, predicates and visit; diagnostics do not imply external resource cancellation.

D0274.name: UndefinedPatch
D0274.rationale: UndefinedPatch is reachable compile-time normalization support; missing/undefined means retain and nullable predicates alone can be explicitly cleared.

D0275.name: GraphWalkStrategy
D0275.rationale: breadthFirst/depthFirst are actual strategy choices, independently configurable from revisit and emission; generic strategy naming is appropriate.

D0276.name: GraphWalkRevisitPolicy
D0276.rationale: once/simplePaths/walks are supported occurrence policies with fixed first-resolution caching; this is genuine configurability rather than aspirational behavior.

D0277.name: GraphWalkLimits
D0277.rationale: Limit names accurately expose accounting units, including end-of-stream attempts and omitted/returning targets; maxDepth alone is not a shortest-radius guarantee under DFS.

D0278.name: GraphWalkRevisitOptions
D0278.rationale: Route modes require a depth/read bound and do not accept admission count alone as safety proof; constructor typing mirrors runtime validation.

D0279.name: GraphWalkRouteContext
D0279.rationale: Route context includes a path only for route modes; once context intentionally omits that capability rather than promising all possible paths.

D0280.name: GraphWalkExpandContext
D0280.rationale: Expansion context supplies occurrence depth and incoming edge; shouldExpand acts after observations and does not suppress already emitted vertex records.

D0281.name: GraphWalkFollowContext
D0281.rationale: Follow context supplies found source and candidate target depth before resolution; its route path is the current source prefix, not an already resolved target path.

D0282.name: GraphWalkExpansionPredicate
D0282.rationale: Expansion predicate really configures expansion policy per occurrence where supported; boolean is validated and topology callbacks remain separate.

D0283.name: AsyncGraphWalkExpansionPredicate
D0283.rationale: Async expansion predicate permits promise booleans without introducing concurrency or cancellation promises; it shares the same occurrence semantics.

D0284.name: GraphWalkEdgePredicate
D0284.rationale: Edge predicate runs before target hydration so rejected links cannot seed cache; this is a genuine pruning control separate from revisit eligibility.

D0285.name: AsyncGraphWalkEdgePredicate
D0285.rationale: Async edge predicate preserves pre-resolution filtering and serial callback policy; it does not make source outgoing enumeration concurrent.

D0286.name: GraphWalkFields
D0286.rationale: Walking fields include source/policies/visitors and execution selectors; nullable predicate clearing and option snapshots justify their configurable names.

D0287.name: AsyncGraphWalkFields
D0287.rationale: Async fields preserve source/hook receiver snapshots and selectable walking policy while excluding unsupported concurrency; strict own-key validation is intentional.

D0288.name: GraphWalkOptions
D0288.rationale: Full graph-walk options combine fields with bounded revisit union; visitors/emission/source mode are genuinely independent, so retain generic family options name.

D0289.name: AsyncGraphWalkOptions
D0289.rationale: Async full walk options add promise/async iterable capability through source/hook types rather than a different graph domain.

D0290.name: GraphWalkOptionsPatch
D0290.rationale: Walking patch allows revisit changes only when merged bounds remain valid; supplied limits replace their record while undefined retains it, as explicitly documented.

D0291.name: AsyncGraphWalkOptionsPatch
D0291.rationale: Async walking patch validates atomically before changing future-runner snapshots; callback policies remain distinct from active runner execution options.

D0292.name: GraphWalkPhase
D0292.rationale: Walking phase enum equals event-kind literals because its callbacks observe those records; no forced equivalence with DAG callback-before-commit phases is appropriate.

D0293.name: GraphWalkRunner
D0293.rationale: Sync walker close terminally disposes resources whereas iterator return pauses; common execution lacks close because tree/DAG sources do not own lazy source iterators.

D0294.name: ResolverTarget
D0294.rationale: ResolverTarget already models optional inline hydration accurately but is private/reachable; export a mode-specific alias to let clients annotate reusable helpers.

D0295.name: InlineOrCachedTarget
D0295.rationale: InlineOrCachedTarget models explicit inline/cache requests; broad exported GraphWalkTarget erases this useful branch distinction for source implementations.

D0296.name: GraphWalkVertex
D0296.rationale: Walking vertex is an ID/data record rather than tree Vertex with hints; its shallow caller data semantics are appropriate for a general information graph.

D0297.name: GraphWalkTarget
D0297.rationale: Public target union covers both hydration policies but cannot annotate mode-specific helper output ergonomically; provide mode-preserving type choices.

D0298.name: LinkTo
D0298.rationale: LinkTo is reachable target-parameterized machinery that could support exported mode-specific links without changing source runtime behavior.

D0299.name: GraphWalkLink
D0299.rationale: GraphWalkLink wraps target plus edge data but defaults to broad target union; users need hydration-preserving aliases for reusable outgoing helpers.

D0300.name: SourceProtocol
D0300.rationale: SourceProtocol ties roots/outgoing to a target parameter correctly; issue lies in accessible annotation aliases, not the generic protocol implementation.

D0301.name: GraphWalkSource
D0301.rationale: GraphWalkSource is a correctly discriminated union enforcing resolver versus inline/cache modes; retain runtime checks and improve public per-mode target/link annotations.

D0302.name: AsyncIterableResult
D0302.rationale: AsyncIterableResult combines promised container with sync/async enumeration; inline resolutions themselves remain tagged values rather than hidden promises.

D0303.name: AsyncSourceProtocol
D0303.rationale: Async protocol retains target-mode coupling while permitting async source iterables; no eager materialization or concurrency is implied.

D0304.name: AsyncGraphWalkSource
D0304.rationale: Async source preserves the same hydration distinction and needs the same accessible mode-specific target/link aliases as sync sources.

D0305.name: GraphWalkVertexResult
D0305.rationale: Walking found/omitted result has no dependency-satisfaction acknowledgment because exploration has no W/C scheduling; retain this scoped omission contract.

D0306.name: GraphWalkVisitor
D0306.rationale: Walking visitor uses domain/domain/phase/ID generic ordering and event payload; optional tree generic alignment must not erase this distinct payload shape.

D0307.name: AsyncGraphWalkVisitor
D0307.rationale: Async walking visitor changes result to MaybePromise but remains serial and phase-specific; keep the event-oriented callback rather than tree Vertex compatibility.

D0308.name: GraphWalkVisitorResult
D0308.rationale: Walking commands deliberately allow only NOOP/pause; mutation, settlement, chain-state and subtree commands reject because those are not this family's capabilities.

D0309.name: GraphWalkVisitorContext
D0309.rationale: Admission and phase-observation indexes separate route occurrence from per-phase records; registration/visitorIndex remain callback metadata rather than task priority.

D0310.name: GraphWalkInspection
D0310.rationale: Walking inspection adds strategy/revisit/frontier/source iterator/observation/request fields to general lifecycle inspection; concurrency literal one truthfully reflects supported behavior.

D0311.name: GraphWalkOutcome
D0311.rationale: Outcome differentiates exhaustion, limited bounds, explicit closure and failure; FINISHED alone is not remote-source completeness, and exact error values are retained.

D0312.name: GraphWalkSummary
D0312.rationale: Summary reports detached counts and terminal outcome without advancing the walker; null outcome before termination is correct despite paused status.

D0313.name: GraphWalkCounts
D0313.rationale: Counts name attempted reads, admitted targets, distinct resolutions, source links and processed observations separately; they intentionally do not equal emitted event counts.

D0314.name: walkGraph
D0314.rationale: walkGraph runs once and returns a resumable runner; caller can configure all relevant strategy/revisit/predicate/selector options through one object.

D0315.name: walkGraphAsync
D0315.rationale: Async walk helper awaits the run boundary and returns the same serial-capability runner, not an unbounded traversal promise detached from pause state.

D0316.name: AsyncGraphWalkRecordSelectors
D0316.rationale: Async record selectors return promised IDs/outgoing iterable relations and explicit root IDs; they materialize into a synchronous reusable source afterward.

D0317.name: materializeWalkSourceFromRecords
D0317.rationale: Walking record materializer returns an actual resolver-mode protocol, so Source naming is correct unlike the DAG input envelope helpers.

D0318.name: materializeWalkSourceFromRecordsAsync
D0318.rationale: Async materialization describes catalog ingestion timing while resulting source remains synchronous resolver mode; no rename to AsyncGraphWalkSource is warranted.

D0319.name: GraphWalkCatalogLink
D0319.rationale: Catalog link uses target ID directly because catalog membership is already captured; lazy GraphWalkLink requires target wrappers and must remain a distinct type.

D0320.name: GraphWalkRecordSelectors
D0320.rationale: Record selectors require explicit roots and outgoing typed edge data, preserving arbitrary ID domains and deterministic root order.

D0321.name: RelationSelection
D0321.rationale: Relation selection includes structural children and separate W/C declaration edges; reachable string union is appropriately scoped to the DAG adapter.

D0322.name: materializeWalkSourceFromDagDefinition
D0322.rationale: DAG-to-walk materializer really configures relation choice and returns a walking protocol; it observes declarations without executing or satisfying their milestones.

D0323.name: GraphWalkDagRelation
D0323.rationale: Adapter-owned relation labels/slot indexes are detached, while caller edge payload identity stays shallow; structural versus W/C relations remain explicit.

ROUTES.name: Package entrypoints, namespace/default routes and metadata
ROUTES.rationale: Reviewed nine runtime entries, package metadata route, namespace/default identity and all binding occurrences; supported VertexRef alias is optional cleanup, while blocked deep imports and nonexported constants/helpers are not public routes.
